query: For lightweight high-entropy alloys intended for weight-critical aerospace and rail-transport applications, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain their ability—or inability—to combine low density with mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance? Specify an unnamed controlled comparison that would test the hypothesis, the observations predicted relative to a baseline alloy, the conditions under which the hypothesis should cease to hold, the existing observations that support it, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In lightweight FCC-based high-entropy alloys (HEAs) that contain ≥12 at.% Al and ≥8 at.% Cr, a percolating population of coherent, nanoscale B2 (NiAl-type) domains forms during low-temperature annealing. 1) The low atomic mass of Al reduces alloy density; 2) the ordered B2 domains impede dislocation glide and block grain-boundary motion, raising both room-temperature and high-temperature strength; 3) Al- and Cr-enrichment within the B2 domains provides a continuous supply of Al and Cr to the alloy surface during exposure to hot, oxidising or saline environments, generating a slow-growing, adherent (Al,Cr)2O3 scale that confers good corrosion and oxidation resistance.  The simultaneous presence and continuity of these B2 domains is therefore the common mechanistic origin of low density + high strength + corrosion/oxidation resistance in such lightweight HEAs.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic (or near-equiatomic) Al15Cr15Fe20Mn20Ni30 high-entropy alloy melted and homogenised, single-phase FCC solid solution with grain size 5-20 µm, no B2 ordering.
generation.intervention: Thermal treatment at 700 °C for 24 h followed by air cooling to promote spinodal decomposition and formation of coherent 5–50 nm B2 (NiAl-type) domains without changing overall composition.
generation.conditions: Mechanical testing at 25 °C and 700 °C in air; cyclic oxidation in flowing air at 800 °C for 100 h; salt-spray corrosion test (ASTM B117) at 35 °C for 168 h.
generation.structural_mediator: Percolating network of coherent 5–50 nm B2 (NiAl-type) domains enriched in Al and Cr, embedded in the FCC matrix.
generation.mechanism: B2 domains (i) supply low-mass Al to reduce density intrinsically, (ii) provide antiphase boundary strengthening and Orowan looping barriers that elevate yield strength, and (iii) act as rapid‐diffusion reservoirs that feed Al and Cr to the surface, establishing a continuous, protective (Al,Cr)2O3 scale that slows oxidation and corrosion.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the quenched, single-phase baseline alloy of identical composition: • 10–30 % higher 0.2 % proof stress at 25 °C and 700 °C. • ≥50 % lower parabolic oxidation rate constant (k_p) during 800 °C exposure. • ≥2× reduction in mass loss or pitting density after 168 h salt-spray. Density remains within ±1 % of baseline because overall composition is unchanged.
generation.baseline: Same alloy quenched from 1200 °C to retain a single-phase FCC random solid solution (no B2 domains).
generation.boundary: Effect should diminish or disappear if (a) Al content <8 at.% or Cr content <5 at.%, (b) grains refined below ≈50 nm (inhibiting coherent domain formation) or coarsened above ≈10 µm (allowing domain coarsening), (c) exposure temperature exceeds ~1000 °C where (Al,Cr)2O3 becomes unstable or B2 dissolves.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of strengthening and oxidation-rate reduction may vary with minor alloying additions (e.g., Ti, V, Mg); the exact continuity requirement for B2 domains is not yet quantified; alternative protective scales (e.g., TiO2) could contribute in some compositions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two specimens of the stated alloy: (1) annealed at 700 °C/24 h (B2-containing); (2) quenched baseline. Confirm B2 presence by TEM/SAED and 3-D atom probe. Measure density (Archimedes), tensile properties at 25 °C and 700 °C, cyclic-oxidation mass gain at 800 °C (thermogravimetry), and post-test oxide chemistry (XPS).
measurements: Parabolic oxidation rate constant k_p (mg^2·cm^-4·s^-1) at 800 °C
Mass change or pit density in ASTM B117 salt-spray test
TEM/B2 domain size and volume fraction
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If B2 domains are confirmed present yet (i) yield strength is ≤ baseline within experimental error OR (ii) oxidation/corrosion rates are not reduced (≤10 % difference) relative to baseline under identical conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.
